lines.en: : Ami, open up. I’m bored.
: Coming! One second, Sensei!
I hear a few drawers slam shut from inside of Ami’s room and wonder what it is she could be doing there.
But before those thoughts go anywhere substantial, the tapping of footsteps racing to the door drags me back to reality.
: Hi! Perfect timing.
: Perfect timing for what, exactly? Because if you're going to make me do something-
: Of course I'm going to make you do something. That’s my job.
: Your job is to cook and clean for me, not force me back into the world when I'm finally able to get away from it.
: Oh, stop. It's not like I'm asking you to do anything serious. I just need you to come grocery shopping with me so Maya stops complaining about not having anything to drink.
: Tell Maya to get her own drinks. She’s scarily independent. I'm sure she can manage.
: She’s also super lazy. And I’m kinda running out of stuff too, so I just figured I'd go for a walk and fix the problem on my own.
: Or at least that's what I was going to do. But now you get to come with me.
: Is anything even open around here this late?
: Mhm! There’s a corner store a few blocks away from here that’ll be open for another thirty minutes or so.
: It's good you showed up when you did, Sensei! You would have missed out on your chance otherwise.
: What is it with you two and getting me to carry stuff across town this late at night?
: It’s not “across town” Sensei, it’s like two blocks-
: Wait. What did you just say?
: I said that you are lucky I'm feeling generous tonight. Because otherwise, I would not do this.
: Okay!
: Let's get a move on, Sensei!
And so the two of us make our way out of the dorms and into the street.
The hot summer air surrounds us, forcing us into a battle in which our respective resolves are tested as we are forced to walk another two blocks to our destination.
One of several things that Ami and I have in common is our mutual hate for extremely hot weather.
So the fact that we have gone out at night, when temperatures are expected to be a bit cooler, and things are still like this?...
Well, that's just fucking annoying.
: Guuuuuuuuuuuhhhhhh...
: Yeah. I feel that.
: Why does it have to be so...sticky and gross outside?
: Whatever happened to cooler summer nights? And who was it that signed us up for this billion degree weather?
: No clue. But I think you and I should probably have a word with them.
: Hey, [amimaster]...
: What would you think about maybe going away somewhere soon?
: I would think that there are multiple problems with that suggestion.
: Problems? Like what?
: Problem A: We can’t leave Kumon-mi.
: Who said we have to leave Kumon-mi? What if it was something simple? Like...the beach? Or an onsen or something?
: Problem B-
: Can we just forget about Problem B and start making plans already?
: No. Because Problem B is that it’s still the middle of the[school] year. When would we even have time to go anywhere?
: It can just be for the weekend or something! Like...maybe we could rent a shack near the beach and all hang out there for a night or two?
: Don't you think it would be nice to get away, Sensei?
: I know you hate this heat just as much as I do...So inside your head, you’re probably all like “Yaaaay water!” or “I finally get to see my [niece] in a swimsuit!” or something like that.
: I am thinking nothing of the sort.
I am.
: In fact, the only thing that's running through my head at the moment is that Maya is going to have to get her own damn groceries next time.
: Especially considering the fact that it looks like the store we're heading to is closing right now.
: Wait, what?! No! Wait for us, old lady! We'll be quick, I promise!
Ami grabs my wrist and drags me to the front of the store with her, forcing me to bow and ask for the old woman to open back up for a few minutes.
The woman obliges and I follow my [niece] as she fills a basket with an assortment of random items that I wind up not paying much attention to.
And before long-
We’re back out in the heat.
: Bleeeeeeeeeeeeh...
: Who even invented weather in the first place? They’re stupid and I want them to know that.
: No one “invented” weather, Ami. That's not a thing I should have to tell you.
: I obviously know that, [amimaster]. I’m not an idiot.
: Sure, I might be bad at math and science and...umm...all of the other subjects we have. But I've got a pretty good head on my shoulders, Sensei.
: Then why are there leeks in your shopping bag? I don't remember them being on the list.
: Wait...yeah. Why are there leeks in my shopping bag?
: How the heck did those even get in there?
: I know the answer.
: Then what-
: I snuck them in while you weren’t looking.
: You...snuck leeks into my basket?
: I did.
: Why?
: Sensei, what kind of weird practical joke is that?
: I think it's less of a joke and more me simply being passively hilarious.
: Your sense of humor is stupid.
: Enjoy your leeks, Ami.
: That aside, did you get everything else you needed?
: Mhm. Soda for me and bunch of random milk tea thingies for Maya.
: You’re stocking up on soda? I figured you'd be a little more conscious about your health.
: It’s fun to do things you know aren’t good for you every once in a while.
: But I’m sure you know all about that...don’t you, [amimaster]?
: Are you really saying what I think you’re saying right now?
: Maybe. What do you think I’m saying?
: That you’ve found out about my secret girlfriend.
: That’s right, I-
: Wait, what?! Who is it?! I’ll kill her! You’re mine!
: I’m kidding, obviously.
: You're referencing how our relationship has progressed past the point of us being just family. Right?
: Heheh...look at us, Sensei...Keeping something so naughty hidden from so many people.
: Are you really trying to seduce me on a park bench just fifty feet away from a woman who sold you leeks a few minutes ago?
: I never wanted these leeks! You did this! This is your fault!
: And also no! I’m just stating facts!
: But...then again...
: I guess you might not think so.
There’s a certain sadness in Ami’s voice that I think I understand.
A type of longing that most could not possibly fathom, but one that makes absolute sense to her.
But...
I can’t do that with her.
The two of us can't be anything more than this.
She’s been through enough already.
She doesn’t need the only person she has left in the world taking advantage of her, even if he wants to.
Which I'm not saying he does.
We just...
We can't be like that.
: Ami.
: Hm?
: Let’s go on a vacation.
: Wait, really?! We can?!
: I was only being half-serious when I suggested it before!
: Oh. Well, if that’s the case-
: No! No take-backs! You said vacation, so I’m getting a vacation whether you like it or not!
: It will have to be somewhere close, obviously. We don't really have the time to go anywhere else.
: Well, yeah. Obviously. Not like we have much of a choice anyway.
: Do you really have enough money to get all of us a place to stay, though?
: All of us?
: Yeah. I mean, Maya and Ayane are coming too, right?
: And if it’s some place like the beach, we might as well just invite the rest of the class too and have a huge vacation trip for everyone.
And here I was thinking this was going to be a thing for just the two of us.
Oh well, I guess. Not like I’m going to say no to hanging out with even more cute girls at once.
If anything, this is even better.
I just hope that having everyone in one place outside of school doesn't lead to any sort of drama.
: Yeah...everyone can come.
: It’s summer, so you should all be enjoying yourselves.
: So should you, Sensei.
: You’ve always got that...tired look in your eyes that makes it seem like you just want to take a break from life.
: Let's hope that a vacation is what you need to pick yourself back up.
: And if it’s not, I can always just give you a big hug instead. As many as you want.
: That would probably work, right [amimaster]?
: Yeah...I guess.
: I think I’ll take the vacation instead, though.
: Be more excited about hugging your [niece], you jerk!
The heat persisted until I dropped Ami back off at the dorm.
It didn't let up until I was already halfway home.
Ami’s affection has increased to [ami_love]!
